The vision inertial odometry component benefits from optimized sliding window computations, which enhance the system’s computational efficiency and numerical stability. Extensive testing on the EUROC and M2DGR datasets, as well as trials using mobile robotic platforms in real-world campus settings, has demonstrated that our multi-sensor fusion system outperforms conventional SLAM systems in accuracy and robustness. These results underscore the system’s potential for navigating and mapping in challenging environments.

articleTitle: A Normalized Risk Comprehensive Evaluation Method for Natural Disaster Areas of Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: Transmission lines are the energy arteries that ensure socio economic development. Conducting a comprehensive evaluation of natural disasters in transmission line areas is of great significance for line safety and socio-economic development. Traditionally, the TOPSIS approach has been widely utilized to achieve comprehensive risk assessment of natural disasters on transmission lines and has attained good performance. However, experiments have shown that there are still exits many challenging factors. Therefore, in this work, a novel method the entropy method (EM) based approach is proposed to improve the performance of the comprehensively evaluate for the road risk of the natural disaster in transmission lines. Existing methods indicate that there are significant differences in the evaluation results corresponding to different evaluation strategies. By analyzing the specific influencing factors that affect the evaluation results, this paper introduces the EM algorithm to propose a new TOPSIS comprehensive evaluation standardization method for road risks in disaster areas. Simulation experiments show that the proposed scheme can achieve the performance significantly.

articleTitle: EEG Classification of Epilepsy Based on Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: The parameter settings of electrical stimulation techniques vary from person to person. Therefore, the transition from a fixed model to an individualized treatment plan is a major challenge in the clinical management of epilepsy. To fully identify the different epileptic states and provide a theoretical basis for individualized treatment, a highly robust Bagging classifier based on decision trees was used to classify the epileptic signals into four categories. First, four features such as standard deviation (Std), coefficient of variation (CV), logarithm of amplitude (Log) and interquartile range (IQR) are extracted from the epileptic signals as inputs to the classifier. Then, the optimal feature was selected by feature comparison experiments and the influence of different frequency bands on classification effect was explored by Discrete Wavelet Transformation (DWT). Five metrics, such as confusion matrix, accuracy, correctness, misclassification rate, and F1 score, are provided as evaluation metrics. Finally, the full-band data featuring Std_IQR gave the best classification with accuracy, precision, false positive rate and F1 score of 94.8864%, 94.9904%, 1.7045% and 94.8947%, respectively. Therefore, the method proposed in this paper can classify interictal, preictal, ictal and postictal epilepsy with high-quality.

articleTitle: Optimization Method for Flexible Dispatch of Source, Grid, Load and Storage Considering Different Photovoltaic Penetration Rates
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: As the scale of grid connection of renewable resources such as wind and solar continues to increase, it is difficult to meet system needs by relying solely on the existing single fast peak-shaving power source. Therefore, this paper aims at the power system scheduling problem under different photovoltaic penetration rates. First, the multi-dimensional characteristics of photovoltaics are modeled. Then, a system scheduling model for the interaction of four types of resources: conventional units, grid elasticity, load response, and energy storage is established. Finally, to minimize the system peak-shaving cost, the optimal system scheduling strategy under different photovoltaic penetration rates is obtained, and the dynamic matching of different photovoltaic penetration rates with the peak-shaving capacity of the power system is completed. A system scheduling strategy that can meet different photovoltaic penetration rates is proposed to ensure the power system’s balance of supply and demand and improve resource utilization.

articleTitle: Point Cloud Completion Network Based on Global Response Normalization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: In the current landscape where 3D point cloud data is applied in autonomous driving, robotic navigation, virtual reality, and building information modeling. The devices for collecting point cloud data have also become increasingly diverse and advanced. However, due to obstacles and other factors, point cloud collection inevitably results in incomplete data, making point cloud completion a critical aspect of point cloud information processing. To enhance accuracy, this paper proposes a new refinement stage in point cloud networks, introducing Global Response Normalization (GRN) into the point cloud refinement phase to improve network performance. This method achieves better feature fusion between point features and global features, effectively increasing the accuracy of point cloud generation in the refinement stage. The proposed method has demonstrated excellent results on the MVP dataset.

articleTitle: Automatic Sleep Staging for Patients with Abnormal Sleep Structure Based on Single-Channel EEG Signal Implemented by Convolution and Self-Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: With the aim of addressing the issue of the massive investment of human resources required for the current work of manual sleep staging in patients with structural abnormalities of sleep, we proposed an automatic sleep stage classification model based on single-channel electroencephalogram signals for the whole-night polysomnograms of 30 patients (16 males, 14 females) with sleep structural abnormalities in this study. The model extracts temporal-domain features from the raw single-channel electroencephalogram signal segments of each 30s epoch by using a convolutional neural network and a self-attention mechanism, and subsequently utilizes a multilayer perceptron to classify the features to accomplish the task of automatic 5 classification of sleep EEG signals. The proposed model achieves a mean classification accuracy of 81.46% and 82.92% on the C3-M2 and C4-M1 EEG channel, respectively. We also explored the effect of the self-attention mechanism on model performance enhancement and demonstrated the effectiveness of the self-attention mechanism for sleep electroencephalogram signal decoding. At the same time, this study provides evidence for the feasibility of deep learning models for the electroencephalogram decoding task in patients with sleep structural abnormalities.

articleTitle: Power System Load Control Platform Architecture and Data Processing Considering Multi-Type Flexible Resource Access
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: Aiming to cope with the complex and variable operation status of the new kind of power system, promote the consumption of new energy, and realize the optimized control of multiple types of resources, a new kind of power system load control platform architecture and data processing method adapted to multiple types of flexible resources is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the characteristics and existing problems of the new power system are introduced. It points out that with the rapid development of large-scale distributed energy and energy storage devices, the power system needs more efficient data processing and flexible control. Then, the paper elaborates on the classification and standardized modeling method of multi-type new energy equipment and realizes efficient processing and sharing of various data types through data classification and fusion technology. Finally, the article proposes an interactive service platform for power supply and demand based on cloud architecture, which supports real-time data collection, storage, analysis, and display, meets grid scheduling and operation management needs, and improves the intelligent scheduling of power grids.

articleTitle: Regression Prediction of Perceptual Integration Capabilities and N270 Component Using Enhanced Electroencephalography Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: This study aims to investigate the brain electrical signals and perceptual integration abilities of pilots in low-visibility flight environments, focusing on the N270 event-related potential (ERP). The N270 occurs approximately 200 to 300 milliseconds after receiving visual stimuli and primarily appears in the parieto-occipital and occipital areas of the brain. It reflects the brain’s activities in processing visual information, attention allocation, emotional processing, and cognitive control, particularly in response to visual stimuli such as faces and facial expressions. To assess and predict pilots’ cognitive abilities under low-visibility conditions, this study designed a new deep learning algorithm called Enhanced Generative Encoder Network(EGEnet). Building on the existing EEGNet model, EGEnet incorporates residual modules, normalization layers, and dropout layers to enhance feature learning capabilities and model stability. Through automated feature extraction and regression prediction, EGEnet effectively evaluates pilots’ perceptual integration abilities. Moreover, EGEnet demonstrates high accuracy and robustness in processing and reconstructing brain electrical data. This study provides a novel method for individual pilot assessment, promoting the development of intelligent and personalized training and technical support based on passive auditory ERP paradigms.

articleTitle: Short-term Power Load Forecasting Method Based on VMD-MSIDBO-KELM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: In light of the challenges posed by randomness, volatility, and limited predictive accuracy in short-term power load forecasting, efforts are directed towards addressing these issues, a VMD-MSIDBO-KELM forecasting model combining variational mode decomposition (VMD) and multi strategy improved dung beetle algorithm is proposed to optimize the kernel limit learning machine (MSIDBO-KELMMSIDBOKELM). The Gaussian mixture model (GMM) is applied for clustering power load data, discerning comparable daily samples across varying weather conditions, and establishing a focused data foundation for forecasting purposes. VMD method is used to stabilize the original power load sequence and decompose it into several sub sequences with strong regularity to reduce the difficulty of forecasting. Furthermore, a KELM prediction model is constructed for each subsequence, and the kernel parameters and regularization coefficients of KELM are optimized using MSIDBO algorithm to improve the prediction performance of the model. Ultimately, the forecasting outcomes of individual subsequences are aggregated to derive the ultimate power load forecasting value. Through the verification and comparative analysis of numerical examples, it is concluded that the proposed VMDMSIDBO-KELM model has better adaptability and prediction accuracy under different weather conditions.

Author Keywords: multi-strategy fusion improved dung beetle optimizer

articleTitle: Numerical Calculation Analysis of Dynamic Electromagnetic Fields in High-speed Electromagnetic Launcher
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: To investigate the spatiotemporal distribution characteristics of the electromagnetic field during the operation of high-speed electromagnetic launcher, a three-dimensional transient electromagnetic field calculation model is established in this paper to solve the electromagnetic field under high-speed motion conditions. Firstly, by combining Maxwell’s equations, dimensional transient electromagnetic field governing equations are derived. Secondly, the calculations are conducted using a finite element-based moving conductivity method. The material properties of the moving region are assigned with varying values based on displacement to simulate the armature, thereby eliminating the issue of oscillatory solutions caused by the rapid movement of grid nodes in traditional finite element methods. The spatiotemporal distribution of the magnetic field during the high-speed motion of the armature is obtained, and a comparative analysis is conducted between the numerical results of the armature in static and moving conditions. The results indicate that during high-speed armature motion, the velocity vortex current term weakens the main current, thus reducing the electromagnetic force. The maximum electromagnetic force calculated using the moving conductivity method is 30.52 kN, approximately 2.2 kN lower than that calculated for a static armature. Furthermore, the maximum magnetic flux density value along the central axis of the dynamic armature is slightly lower than that of the static armature, which is experimentally verified to be closer to the actual launch state. This study provides a data foundation for the unified design method of electromagnetic comprehensive performance and reliability of electromagnetic energy equipment under extreme conditions.

articleTitle: Overview of SAR Image Fusion Processing Techniques with Other Sensor Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR), with its all-weather and all-day operational capabilities and wide-area detection ability, has become an important means for global monitoring of terrain and oceans. The fusion processing of SAR images with other sensor data can fully utilize the complementary advantages of information from various sensors to obtain richer and more targeted fusion results. This paper first analyzes and summarizes the SAR and opticalimage fusion processing techniques, including the main methods of pixel-level, feature-level, and decision-level fusion; then introduces the SAR and Automatic Identification System (AIS) data fusion processing technology, including data association methods based on location feature information and basedon multi-feature fusion, as well as ship fusion detection and recognition methods; finally, it summarizes the aforementioned methods.

articleTitle: Adaptive Heterogeneous Dual Ant Colony System Based on Population Information Similarity for the Traveling Salesman Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: In order to deal with the slow convergence speed of ant colony algorithm and the conflicting issues of exploration and exploitation during the optimization phase of the algorithm, this paper proposes an adaptive heterogeneous dual population ant colony algorithm based on the similarity of the populations (AHDACS). The AHDACS algorithm is composed of sub ant colonies with different characteristics which have potential complementarity. In the process of co-evolution, the pheromone updating strategy of ant colony system is adaptively adjusted according to the change of population information similarity of ant colony system, and the cycle exchange of information between the two populations is automatically adjusted according to population similarity to improve the quality of optimization solutions while maintaining a good balance between rapid convergence speed and searching ability. The designed strategy is used to raise the algorithm’s solution accuracy, accelerate the convergence speed of the algorithm, and increase the ability to exit the local optimal. The traveling salesman problem (TSP) is used to validate and assess the performance of the developed AHDACS. The results of experiments attest that the developed AHDACS exhibits a noticeable enhancement in both convergence speed and optimization capacity, while also effectively balancing the conflict between population diversity and convergence speed.

articleTitle: Receding Horizon Control Based Real-time Strategy for Missile Pursuit-evasion Game
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: This paper presents a solution to the online missile pursuit-evasion game (PEG) problem in a two-dimensional plane. A relative kinematic model of engagement is developed, and a game decision algorithm based on receding horizon control (RHC) is introduced. This algorithm converts the complex maneuvering decision problem into solving the optimal control sequence over a finite future time horizon. In addition, an algorithm based on iterative double optimization is proposed to approximate the Nash equilibrium solution for the PEG. This algorithm avoids the dimensionality catastrophe that occurs when searching for the global Nash equilibrium by seeking a local solution. Finally, simulations were conducted assuming opponents to be either uncontrolled uniform-speed players or intelligent maneuvering players. The strategy’s performance was then compared across different scenarios. The results show that the proposed method successfully integrates local approximation and rolling optimization benefits, enabling real-time strategy planning for PEG with enhanced performance.

articleTitle: Research on the Coordination Method of Scaled Flexible Load Participation in Power System Source-grid Interaction Considering Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for scaled flexible loads to participate in power system source-grid interaction coordination considering uncertainty. By constructing an analytical model of demand response degree based on electricity price and an optimal decision model of source-load interaction coordination and proposing relevant solution algorithms, the paper aims to provide scheduling and control strategies for the future participation of generalized distributed energy storage units in the new energy consumption and capacity support of the power grid. The study includes the architecture and scenarios of source-grid interaction of scaled flexible loads participating in the power system, the establishment and modification of the analytical model of the degree of demand response, and the solution of the coordinated decision-making model of flexible load interaction. The analysis of examples shows that the method significantly improves the dispatch flexibility of the power system and the capacity for new energy consumption.

articleTitle: Multi-time Scale Resources Aggregation Demand Response Potential Assessment Method with Stacked Autoencoder
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: As the global energy transition deepens and the proportion of renewable energy increases, power grids’ reliability, flexibility, and economy face new challenges. A multi-time scale resources aggregation demand response potential assessment method with the Stacked Autoencoder (SAE) techniques is proposed in this paper. The virtual power plants (VPPs) model is for integrating distributed energy resources, promoting renewable energy use, and reducing carbon emissions. The features from adjustable resource electricity data at specific time points based on Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD) and SAE are decomposed and extracted to determine the response capability and uncertainty factors of adjustable resources at each time point. This allows us to construct the probability distribution of the cluster’s response potential at multiple time points. Simulation results show that the proposed method can effectively handle multi-time scale resource aggregation problems.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Game Scheduling Strategy Based on Improved Wolf Pack Algorithm and Hybrid Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: The traditional power grid is significantly transforming to develop new power systems. Traditional demand response methods based on price and incentives are relatively single, unable to fully leverage flexible resources for grid scheduling, smooth peak-valley differences, and ensure the safe and stable operation of the grid. This paper proposes a multi-objective game scheduling strategy based on the improved wolf pack algorithm and hybrid demand response. Flexible resource users engage in a game with grid operators based on a combination of price and incentive demand response, and the improved wolf pack algorithm is used to determine the optimal time-of-use electricity price. Case studies validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: User-side Abnormal Power Consumption Detection Method Based on High-dimensional Random Matrix
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: To accurately grasp the abnormal electricity usage behavior of users on the distribution network side, the application of user electricity risk hazard identification feature extraction and recognition technology is used to achieve a sense of security in electricity usage and a strategy for intelligent, digital user electricity risk early warning push services is proposed. The collected power grid operation data is analysed and modeled based on the random matrix theory. By characterizing the statistical properties of the matrix, the power consumption information is visualized, and a method for identifying abnormal power consumption and meter faults is proposed. This method analyses the fluctuation characteristics of the eigenvalues and gives the specific steps for applying the random matrix theory to the location of abnormal areas of user power consumption. It can also realize the feature discovery of abnormal power consumption points on the user side and then determine abnormal power consumption behavior. The case study shows that this method is highly reliable and accurate.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of the Regolith Sampling Digital Twin System for Operation and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: The exploration of lunar regolith sampling presents challenges such as enhancing intuitive situation awareness, facilitating systematic data analysis, improving operational efficiency, and addressing personnel training complexities under teleoperation conditions. To tackle these issues, we developed a digital twin system for the operation and analysis of regolith sampling. This innovative system incorporates multi-scenario simulations, comprehensive data analytics, and real-time, data-driven decision-making capabilities, augmented by 3D visualization technology. It provides decision-makers with a real-time, accurate depiction of the regolith sampling status, enabling precise analysis and evaluation of detector conditions and the sampling process. By enhancing operational precision and optimizing control over the sampling process, the system has been successfully implemented in China’s Chang’e-6 lunar surface sampling mission. It has delivered significant improvements in situation awareness, process analysis, and decision-making support, thereby markedly elevating the efficiency of regolith sampling operations.

articleTitle: Virtual Inertia Estimation of New Energy Power System Based on WRARMAX Model and LSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: In order to precisely monitor the inertia of power systems, it is crucial to fulfill two key goals. Firstly, the inertia identification model should have a minimal computational time. Secondly, the accuracy of the outcomes must be enhanced. This study introduces the WRARMAX model, which is an Autoregressive Moving Average model with exogenous input solved using Weighted Recursive Least Squares, to expedite the initial phase of model identification. Additionally, the incorporation of multithreaded parallel processing in the code further accelerates the identification process. For the subsequent phase, the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network is utilized to refine the residuals from the initial results, thus enhancing the correlation between the derived inertia values and their actual values. The integration of these two strategies leads to a more rapid and precise inertia identification process, surpassing the efficacy of prior techniques.

articleTitle: Optimal Power System Scheduling Considering Uncertainty-Induced Generation Unit Output Curtailment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: Under the call of the national “dual carbon” goals, the growth of the proportion of new energy generation has become an inevitable trend in energy structure adjustment. The “static parameter” model, which traditional thermal power units rely on, can no longer accurately reflect their output uncertainty, urgently requiring a new optimization scheduling strategy to cope with this change. This study proposes an optimized scheduling model for power generation systems that considers the output curtailment and unplanned outages of thermal power units. It employs non-parametric kernel density estimation techniques to model the uncertainty of thermal power unit output and uses chance constraints to define the fluctuation range of generation output and the system’s reliability. The model adopts a scenario generation method based on Copula theory to construct output scenarios and further employs reduction techniques to optimize the number of scenarios. Moreover, this paper introduces Conditional Value at Risk as a key indicator to measure the cost of system uncertainty risk, thereby providing a more comprehensive perspective in risk assessment. Simulation experiments on the IEEE 30-node standard system demonstrate that compared to traditional optimization scheduling models relying on static parameters, the proposed model can more effectively balance the output fluctuations of different thermal power units, significantly reducing the risk of curtailment due to supply shortages. This study offers a new theoretical basis and practical guidance for optimizing the scheduling of power systems under the context of large-scale integration of new energy and economic fluctuations.

articleTitle: Robust Decision Making with Multi-modal Perception for Autonomus Driving in Hybrid Action Space
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: Making decisions about lateral-lane changes and longitudinal car-following behavior is essential for implementing Autonomous Driving in dynamic and complex traffic environments. The existing techniques may not perform well due to the uncertainty and complexity of the lane-changing case because they only took into account straight paths, incomplete environmental observability, and incomplete optimization goals. To address these issues, we introduced Soft Actor Critic in parameterized action space for Robust Decision making framework in multimodal perception environment. We integrate Hierarchical graphical based embeddings to obtain latent feature vector from multimodal perception, and then use Parameterize Deep Reinforcement Learning in order to get maximum reward in hybrid action space. The results of the experiments indicate that the proposed technique performed well in both macroscopic and microscopic evaluation.

articleTitle: Carbon Emission Calculation and Low Carbon Transition Path Optimization Method for Electric Power Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: With economic development, the energy and power industry must balance power supply growth and carbon reduction requirements. To achieve the goal of“double carbon”, the power system needs to be transformed into green and low-carbon, and accurate carbon emission accounting has become a critical support. Due to the significant differences between cities and regions, emission reduction strategies vary. To this end, the article firstly clarifies the carbon emission accounting boundary of power generation enterprises, establishes a carbon emission accounting model for the power industry based on the IPCC inventory method of fuel consumption, and secondly constructs an enterprise low-carbon transition planning model by integrating technological, economic, environmental and other factors, researches and analyzes the path of power generation enterprises to achieve carbon-neutral transition by 2060, and simulates different low-carbon transition scenarios. The results show that achieving carbon neutrality appropriately in advance is beneficial to power generation enterprises to a certain extent, but advancing the process of carbon neutrality too early will lead to soaringcosts. In addition,future policies will push forward the scale of installed energy storage, and enterprises should make good use of technical and resource reserves. The power industry needs to formulate appropriate low-carbon transformation strategies according to its reality to ensure that it realize a win-win situation regarding economic and social benefits while realizing the goal of carbon neutrality.

articleTitle: Improved Multi-head Bi-directional Long and Short-term Memory Temporal Convolutional Network for Lithium-ion Batteries State of Charge Estimation in Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries with their high voltage, large capacity, high discharge rate, no memory effect, and green environmental protection advantages are widely used in communication, power stations, backup power, and other energy storage fields. Accurate estimation of the state of charge (SOC) of lithium-ion batteries is a key prerequisite to ensure the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of battery systems. To address this core challenge, this paper innovatively proposes a composite model combining the Kepler optimization algorithm, temporal convolutional network (TCN), bi-directional long and short-term memory network (BiLSTM), and multi-head attention mechanism (MHA). Kepler optimization algorithm was used to search the optimal hyperparameters in the TCN-BiLSTM structure so that the model could adjust the structural parameters and extract the input features accurately under different working conditions and temperatures. The multi-head self-attention mechanism is introduced to assign different weights to the feature outputs extracted by time convolution according to the different importance of information to improve the adaptability of the model. Finally, the proposed model is tested and compared with other models under different temperatures and working conditions.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Provincial local Coordinated Based on Source-grid-load-storage Interactions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: Considering the characteristics of coordination among source-network-load-storage, a provincial local coordinated scheduling method based on the interaction of sourcenetwork-load-storage is proposed. Firstly, the interaction mechanism of source-grid-load-storage is refined. Secondly, according to the spatial characteristics of the scheduling of provincial local coordinated, a multi-objective optimal scheduling model is established with the objectives of economy and new energy consumption. Thirdly, a genetic algorithm is used to solve the problem. Finally, by analyzing the examples, it is proved that the proposed method can reduce the system cost and improve the utilization rate of new energy.

articleTitle: Whale-Optimization-Algorithm-Based Virtual Inertia LQR Control for New Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: As the share of renewable energy sources in the electrical grid expands, the system’s inertia and resilience to disturbances are impacted. Unlike traditional synchronous generators, renewable sources such as wind and solar power, along with energy storage systems, lack inherent inertia. This absence can diminish the grid’s inertial capacity, potentially undermining its stability. However, by integrating a virtual inertia control mechanism into these renewable sources, they can emulate the inertial response of conventional machines, thus supporting the system’s stability. This paper delves into the development of a virtual inertia control strategy for renewable energy, utilizing the Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR) algorithm. Through the analysis of virtual synchronous machines’ dynamics, the study derives quantitative measures for inertial parameters and the system’s frequency response. Additionally, a whale-optimizationalgorithm-based is employed to refine the LQR’s control parameters, aiming to enhance the control performance. The article concludes with simulation experiments that confirm the efficacy and practicality of the proposed control approach.

articleTitle: Resilience Assessment of Distributed Distribution Networks Taking into Account Sudden Natural Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: Understanding and improving the reliability of distribution grids under extreme weather conditions in the context of global climate change is important for ensuring stable socio-economic operation and improving the quality of life of the public. The current global assessment of distribution grid reliability under extreme weather conditions faces challenges such as insufficient data, modeling limitations, insufficient consideration of multidimensional impacts, technical resource constraints, and global change uncertainty. Through this paper, we hope to provide new perspectives and ideas for power system researchers and practitioners to jointly explore effective strategies for distribution network reliability and resilience under extreme weather. This study enhances the resilience assessment of distribution networks. It takes into account the generation and consumption dynamics of the network, the unpredictability of power supply and demand, as well as the impact of network topology and equipment on its reliability, and utilizes the Markov process to perform comprehensive reliability analysis of the network. In terms of assessment techniques, the Monte Carlo simulation method simulates the stochastic nature of severe weather, including its severity, timing, and duration, while quantifying its impact on the network through fault modeling. In terms of assessment metrics, the network is divided into two phases in order to establish a precise and clear system of network resilience assessment metrics. Through literature review, modeling analysis, and actual case studies, the current status of distributed generation application in extreme weather is explored, its impact on distribution network reliability is assessed, and future research directions and practical suggestions are proposed.

articleTitle: Phase-Field Simulation of Energy Storage Properties of NaNbO3 Thin Films
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: The phase field model of NaNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> thin films is constructed on the basis of the phase field model, and the influence of mismatch strain on the domain structure of NaNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> thin films is simulated. The results show that compressive strain can make the in-plane domains flip to out-plane domains, while tensile strain can promote the formation of in-plane domains. At the same time, the P-E loops of NaNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> thin films under different misfit strains are simulated to explore the relationship between misfit strain and storage properties of thin films. When the type of strain within the film changes from compressive strain to tensile strain, the residual polarization and coercive electric field of thin films decrease, which is beneficial to obtain higher storage density. However, excessive tensile strain will lead to the decrease of saturation polarization and storage density. The present study complements previous studies using XRD as well as RSM method on the mismatch strain of NaNbO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> ferroelectric thin films in terms of theory, showing excellent theoretical research value in the field of energy storage.

articleTitle: Self-Healing Optimization of Power Grid under High Penetration of New Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: In order to address the problem of high penetration of new energy into the grid, which brings huge intermittency and volatility to the distribution network, and to overcome the shortcomings of the traditional methods such as genetic algorithm and whale algorithm, which are limited and unable In order to construct the most suitable scenarios, this paper considers a distribution network system containing a significant quantity of distributed photovoltaic energy under a high penetration rate. It then builds a stochastic planning model for self-healing of the distribution network by constructing constraint functions and objective functions. The construction of the constraint function and objective function enables the development of a self-healing stochastic planning model for the distribution network. This model is solved using the scenario tree stochastic method and the improved PSO algorithm. Finally, the feasibility of the self-healing optimization method proposed in this paper is verified by applying it to four typical scenarios to demonstrate the limitations of the traditional method. In brief, the methodologies presented in this paper offer superior alternatives to traditional methods. The optimization solution is more expedient and precise, with a discernible positive impact on the self-repair capability of the distribution network and secure operation.

articleTitle: Assessment of Attention Allocation Based on EEGEOG Bimodal Signals
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of individual attention allocation on task performance during concurrent task execution and proposes a bimodal approach to estimate attention allocation levels. A parallel task experimental paradigm, comprising two distinct tasks, was designed. Twelve participants were recruited for the experiment, during which electroencephalography (EEG), electrooculography (EOG), eye-tracking, and key press behavior data were simultaneously recorded. Attention allocation indicators and task performance indicators were derived from the eye-tracking and key press behavior data, and their relationship was analyzed. Additionally, features were extracted from EEG and EOG data, and regression models were applied to estimate attention allocation levels. The experimental results indicate a positive correlation between attention allocation for one task and task performance in concurrent tasks. Furthermore, the attention allocation estimation method that integrates power spectral density (PSD) and EOG features into a gradient boosting regression (GBR) model outperforms other methods. These findings demonstrate the predictability of task performance through attention allocation and validate the feasibility of our bimodal approach for assessing attention allocation.

articleTitle: Six-Dimensional Digital Twin Framework for Coal Fired Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: Data optimization is a key essential for the digital twin system of coal-fired power plant, but existing digital twin frameworks fail to reflect it well. Meanwhile, a systematic hierarchical analysis of the enabling methods and technologies in digital twin is not found in previous literature. To fill these gaps, this paper proposes a six-dimensional digital twin framework for coal-fired power plant and analyzes the relevant enabling methods and technologies from a system level perspective. First, combining the data optimization center with physical system, virtual model, communication link, knowledge base & database, and application & decision center, a six-dimensional digital twin framework for coal-fired power plant is established to fully reflect the importance of data optimization for the power plant digital twin. Then, based on the established framework, common enabling methods are analyzed and classified from the system hierarchy and module functionality perspectives to clarify the different roles and tasks that these methods undertake in digital twin. The framework proposed in this paper aims to provide reference for the practical application of digital twin in coal-fired power plants.

Author Keywords: digital twin enabling methods and technologies

articleTitle: Multimodal Emotion Recognition based on the Fusion of EEG Signals and Eye Movement Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: Emotion recognition research plays a crucial role in advancing brain-computer interfaces. However, many current methods either rely on a single modal signal or use a multimodal fusion approach that may not fully consider the balance of information between modalities. In this study, we propose a novel multimodal emotion recognition method that combines electroencephalograph (EEG) signals and eye movement data using a cosine loss fusion approach. To extract deep features from the two modalities, we utilize ResNet 18 with a gated attention mechanism for EEG feature extraction, and DenseNet for eye movement data feature extraction. The cosine loss function is employed to address inter-modal differences and ensure a balanced fusion of information. Our proposed method achieves an impressive classification accuracy of $91.16 \%$ for the emotions of happiness, fear, sadness, and neutrality on the SEED-IV dataset. This outperforms both EEG signals (74.48%) and eye movement data $(68.38 \%)$, demonstrating the effectiveness of our approach in emotion recognition tasks.

articleTitle: Optimal Energy Scheduling for Microgrids with a Hybrid Battery-Hydrogen Storage System Based on Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: This paper explores the integration of battery and hydrogen storage in a Microgrid (MG), combining the high-power capabilities of battery with the high-capacity characteristics of hydrogen storage to manage instantaneous load variations and balance peak-valley energy differences. The scheduling method employs the Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (TD3) algorithm, recognizing the complexity of the integrated energy system. 24-hour simulations are conducted for representative days across the four seasons—spring, summer, autumn, and winter. The TD3 algorithm minimizes fluctuations in power exchanges with the main grid by effectively synchronizing the operations of battery and Hydrogen Storage System (HSS), thus enhancing grid stability. It learns the patterns between load demands and renewable energy generation, favoring battery charging and hydrogen production during low demand periods and discharging or utilizing hydrogen for electricity during peak demand. This strategy promotes more effective utilization of renewable resources. Additionally, a comparison with the Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm shows that while the cost-related performance for both TD3 and DDPG is nearly identical, TD3 demonstrates significantly better stability, with standard deviations consistently lower than those of DDPG. In particular, under winter conditions, the standard deviation of TD3 is only 45.5% of that of DDPG.

articleTitle: Similarity Analysis of an Air-bearing Simulator Reproducing Drag-free Control Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: This paper introduces a design model of the ground spacecraft simulator to emulate the drag-free satellite. The simulator model is composed of an air bearing testbed and two inverted pendulums. On the basic of equivalent mass and equivalent stiffness, the dynamic model of the simulator is derived from the Euler-Lagrange method. And the dynamic equivalence conditions between two systems are expressed as the scaling laws. Subsequently, the similarity analysis is performed by using analytic hierarchy process. The similarity elements and corresponding characteristic variables are put forward to establish the proper evaluation model system. Finally, the similarity analysis of ground model simulation is given. The high system similarity degree can prove the rationality and effectiveness of the design method.

articleTitle: Wind Farm Power Optimization Using Bayesian Adaptive Direct Search for Active Pitch Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: The rapid development of the wind energy sector, particularly in China, has led to significant advancements towards carbon neutrality and renewable energy utilization. However, optimizing wind farm control strategies to enhance power output and economic efficiency remains a critical challenge, particularly in mitigating wake effects between turbines. This study focuses on addressing these challenges through the implementation of active pitch control strategies. The Bayesian-Adaptive Direct Search (BADS) algorithm, which combines the global search capabilities of Bayesian Optimization with the local refinement strengths of Mesh Adaptive Direct Search, is utilized for real-time optimization. This method effectively navigates the high-dimensional parameter space, accommodating non-smooth pitch angle settings and complex thrust coefficient curves. Open-FAST, from the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL), serves as the primary simulation tool. Through simulations conducted on three NREL 5MW turbines, the proposed strategy demonstrated a $4.7 \%$ increase in total power output by effectively reducing wake effects and enhancing energy utilization. This research not only highlights the inadequacies of current parameter control and optimization methods but also presents a viable solution for improving wind farm performance.

articleTitle: Visualization Method of Emotional EEG Features Based on Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: In recent years, deep learning models have been increasingly applied in emotional brain computer interfaces. Unlike traditional emotional brain computer interfaces, they perform end-to-end learning on raw EEG signals and use Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) to analyze emotional EEG signals, which has become a commonly used method in this field. However, due to the fact that CNN is a black box model, the decision-making process between them is not visible, and the decoding process of the model cannot be understood, resulting in poor interpretability of the model and difficulty in convincing the predicted results. Based on the above issues, three different architectures of CNN models were designed, named shallow CNN, middle CNN, and deep CNN according to the depth of the convolutional layers, and three visualization methods were used to improve the interpretability of the CNN model. Visualizing the features learned in the five EEG frequency bands of the midlevel CNN using spectral power difference, it was found that the Delta, Beta, and Gamma EEG frequency bands may be closely related to emotions, with active areas mainly appearing in the frontal, temporal, and occipital regions of the brain. By studying the maximum activation method, the output feature maps of the shallow CNN with the lowest classification performance and the middle CNN with the highest classification performance were visualized. The results showed that the middle CNN had a higher degree of activation and was more sensitive to capturing emotional information.

articleTitle: Voltage Control Method for Offshore Floating Photovoltaic Storage Hydrogen Production DC System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: To address the problems of high PV output volatility and unstable DC system voltage control caused by environmental influences on offshore floating photovoltaic hydrogen production systems, this paper proposes a voltage control method based on voltage stabilization for the DC system model of PV storage hydrogen production. Aiming to improve PV power generation quality and enhance system stability, this control method includes maximum power point tracking (MPPT) control for the floating PV system and adaptive coordinated control for the hydrogen storage system. These controls enable the optimal utilization of light resources while ensuring stable bus voltage. Finally, the effectiveness of the control method was verified by simulation.

articleTitle: Parameter Identification of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor with Improved Spider Monkey Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: The traditional spider monkey algorithm (SMO) has some problems in the identification of permanent magnet synchronous motor parameters, such as slow convergence speed, easy to fall into local optimal and unstable identification results. In this paper, an improved Spider monkey algorithm combined with chaotic mapping learning strategy (TSMO) is proposed. The chaotic mapping learning strategy was used to expand the distribution of the initial population, which can improve the algorithm’s global and local search capability. The TMSO algorithm was employed in parametric experiments on permanent magnet synchronous motors to assess the efficacy of the enhanced algorithm. which is more expeditious, precise, and reliable than other algorithms for parameter identification.

articleTitle: MSRUNet: Multiscale Residual U-Net Network for Spine MRI Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: Spinal medical images are essential for clinicians to diagnose spinal conditions. Computer segmentation can often be utilized to assist physicians in making a diagnosis, but traditional segmentation methods are time-consuming. Recently, deep learning has become more prevalent in medical imaging. This paper introduces a high-performance automatic segmentation method for spinal MRI images using deep learning. The proposed method, called multiscale residual UNet (MSRUNet), enhances the classical U-Net architecture by incorporating residual double convolution and a customized ASPP block. These improvements allow the model to accurately focus on and segment various tissue and lesion regions in MRI images. This study assesses the model’s performance on SpineSagT2Wdataset3 by measuring its recall, accuracy, Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) and Intersection over Union (IoU) metrics. Compared to other models, including U-Net, MSRUNet showed superior segmentation performance, demonstrating its effectiveness. This work advances automated spine MRI segmentation and promotes automated diagnosis and treatment of spinal disorders.

articleTitle: Residual Capacity Estimation with Incremental Learning for Lithium-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: Accurately estimating the state of health (SOH) for lithium-ion batteries based on their residual capacity is essential for future intelligent battery management systems. However, the absence of complete charge-discharge data presents significant challenges in developing an accurate and reliable SOH estimation model. To address this issue, we propose a closedloop battery residual capacity (BRC) estimation method using an incremental learning-based model that can be re-trained during most practical charging operations. Initially, an optimal voltage range is selected using a multi-objective particle swarm optimization algorithm based on the correlation between partial charging capacity (PCC) and BRC, as well as the initial voltage data distribution during the charging process. Unlike traditional BRC estimation methods, support vector regression quickly characterizes the mapping using degradation features and PCC. A linear BRC estimation model is then established based on the relationship between PCC and BRC. Using continuous updates in online monitoring data, adaptive training with online learning is used to enhance the prediction performance of the BRC estimation model. By implementing incremental learning technology, we construct a closed-loop model that improves as more observation data is collected. An analysis of an open-source dataset demonstrates that the proposed SOH estimation method achieves satisfying and robust results in estimating the BRC.

articleTitle: Cooperative Optimal of Source-network-load-storage Dispatch of New Power Systems Under The Dual-Carbon Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 25th China Conference on System Simulation Technology and its Application (CCSSTA)
abstract: With the proposal of the dual-carbon strategy, the transition to a low-carbon energy system has become a widely recognized development direction. But this transition is also accompanied by many new problems and tests. Taking into account the interdependence of elastic regions, to solve the contradiction between the growing demand for flexibility systems and the unbalanced distribution of flexibility resource, a new power system source-network-storage collaborative planning method is proposed. Firstly, under the careful consideration of various power generation technologies, energy storage and demand response, a collaborative optimization model based on dual carbon targets for a new power system is established to achieve the lowest total cost. Then, convert the policy requirements of the dual-carbon targets, renewable energy penetration rate, wind and light abandonment rate into constraints and integrate them into the power generation planning model. Besides, the paper introduces relaxation variables to eliminate constraints and builds the initial basic solution to iterative optimization. Finally, the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method are verified by simulation.
